Coastal city, imagined study

City After the Rain.

An editorial exploration of what rain reveals about streets, infrastructure and the spaces between buildings.

Theme
Water and density

Format
Editorial concept

Study
Imagined

After rainfall, the city reads differently. Pavements reflect their surroundings and ordinary drainage routes become visible.

Rather than treating water as an interruption, this imagined study looks at the streets, edges and thresholds that help a dense city absorb it.

Every street is also a landscape.

Courtyards, planted margins and permeable surfaces can change how a place handles water. The design question is not simply where rain goes, but what it leaves behind.
